svg.text: A packed module is reduced to a few representative cells, each solved on its own share, then swept over design choices.
Coolant warms along the channel, so outlet cells
run hottest; cells on the wall see a different
boundary. Each design is judged on four cells:
interior and edge, at the inlet and the outlet.
filler: PCM, PCM + graphite or air
cooling: side ribbon (or bottom plate, or air)
interior cell's share (unit cell) → circle of equal area
edge cell: part of its share lies on the module wall
Jelly roll: heat q‴(t) from the
Cooling sink: heat leaves into coolant at Tc(t), set by
the coolant's own heat balance along the channel.
Air cooling wets the whole can, so 1D fits. A plate
or a ribbon touches one side, so those run in 2D (D).
WLTC, motorway + rapid charge, constant C-rate
interior and edge × inlet and outlet
mass vs fan / pump / chiller energy,
Where cooling touches one side: 2D slices of the same share
Heat runs down the winding to the plate,
so the top of the cell runs hottest.
symmetry plane: half the can is solved
The ribbon touches a strip of the can, so heat
runs round the can to reach it.
Both slices share one solver with the 1D model:
finite volumes in enthalpy form, so the PCM melts
and re-freezes, with the same cell heat, coolant
The 2D field changes the answer: the plate case
runs about 6 K hotter at the top than at the base
at the 1.5C peak, which a 1D model cannot see.
Schematic, not to scale. ru: radius of a circle with the same area as one cell's share.
